task.description: Design a fix for ISS-0343 per step-01's diagnosis: Backfill.run/1 sweeps ALL tenants' Registration rows and calls Registry.register_type/2 per tenant; under scripts/test_parallel.sh, a concurrently-running test's teardown (DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE, uncoordinated by any lock) can drop a different tenant's physical schema in the window between Backfill.run/1 reading that tenant's Registration row and Registry's query executing against it, producing an uncaught Postgrex undefined_table exception ('relation tenant_*.event_type_registry does not exist') that crashes the whole backfill sweep. Design a fix per step-01's next_action direction: make the missing-schema case a typed, tolerated skip rather than a crash, scoped narrowly to the diagnosed race (do not scope Backfill.run/1 to a single tenant -- that changes its intended all-tenants production semantics; do not rely solely on locking test fixture teardown -- that doesn't close the query-layer gap). Write lib/letflow/design/iss0343-backfill-missing-schema-tolerance.md: exact error shape/typed reason to add, exactly which Registry.ex functions/call sites detect and translate the Postgrex exception, how Backfill.run/1's Enum.reduce_while/3 handles the new outcome (as skipped, not halted), and confirmation this doesn't change Backfill.run/1's public arity/contract. Design only -- no implementation code.
acceptance_criteria: design doc maps step-01's diagnosed race to a concrete typed error shape (distinct from :tenant_not_provisioned) added to Registry's affected function specs
design doc identifies the exact call sites (current_max query, insert, get_type query) that must detect the missing-schema condition and how (Postgrex.Error postgres.code match, not a blanket rescue)
design doc specifies Backfill.run/1's new case clause treats the condition as skipped (not halted), with no change to its public @spec/arity
design doc explicitly states why scoping Backfill.run/1 to a single tenant_id, and why locking only the test fixture's DROP SCHEMA, are not chosen as the fix (or are noted as insufficient alone)
no implementation code (.ex code blocks) present -- signatures/specs/shapes in prose or @spec-style typespec blocks only

result.summary: Design written to lib/letflow/design/iss0343-backfill-missing-schema-tolerance.md. Chosen fix: tolerate a concurrently-vanished tenant schema as a typed, non-crashing outcome at the Registry query layer rather than scoping Backfill.run/1 to one tenant or relying solely on fixture-side locking. Adds a new Registry error reason {:error, :tenant_schema_missing} (distinct from :tenant_not_provisioned: the Registration row exists, but the physical schema Postgres holds does not) to register_type/2's and get_type/2's specs (validate_payload/3 inherits it transitively via its existing forwarded-error shape). Detection is a new private rescue_missing_schema/1 helper in Letflow.EventStore.Registry that narrowly rescues %Postgrex.Error{postgres: %{code: :undefined_table}} (re-raising anything else unchanged) around three call sites: insert_with_monotonicity_check/2's current_max query and its Repo.insert/2 call, and get_type/2's Repo.one/2 query. Letflow.TenantProvisioning.Backfill.run/1 gains one new case clause (alongside the existing :tenant_not_provisioned clause) that logs a warning and counts the tenant as skipped, not halted -- Backfill.run/1's own @spec and all-tenants sweep semantics are unchanged. Section 4 explicitly weighs and rejects, as the primary fix, both scoping Backfill.run/1 to a single tenant_id (would remove real ISS-0332 production behavior to patch a test-only symptom) and advisory-locking only TenantFixture's teardown DROP SCHEMA (would narrow just the test-fixture instance of the race without closing the query-layer gap Backfill.run/1 itself exposes against any schema that vanishes for any reason mid-sweep). One open question flagged for ELIXIR-DEV: confirm at implementation time that :undefined_table is the exact postgrex atom for SQLSTATE 42P01 rather than assuming it from the mnemonic. No implementation code included -- typespecs, prose control-flow, and a file-touch list only.
